FVD specifies a 47.5 mm compressor inlet for its K16/24 conversion and describes changes to the housing contour, backplate and thrust bearing. The exact donor identity, complete wheel dimensions and compressor/turbine maps were not established by this product page.
The FVD page states a balancing process reaching 100,000 rpm. This describes a manufacturing test condition. It does not specify the maximum continuous operating speed of the 993 turbo.

FVD advertises 555 hp when its turbo upgrade is combined with its software, intercoolers and supporting components. The page does not supply a measured 993 operating-point set, compressor map or turbine map. The unit hp is retained as published.

TTH offers a conversion using supplied original Porsche/BorgWarner K16 cores with size-8 hot housings. It advertises up to 650 PS with appropriate engine components and recalibration. It provides no measured map, operating speed envelope or test configuration on the consulted page.
TTH reports a balance figure of 0.05 g. The page does not identify the associated radius, residual-unbalance unit such as g mm, speed-dependent acceptance limits or balance grade.

The TTH 750 PS product is based on K24 donors with size-10 hot housings. It is a different donor route from the K16-650 product, and its advertised power depends on engine components and software changes.

TTE describes the 993 TTE650 5050 as an upgrade of the original K16/8 pair. It specifies a 50 mm compressor inlet with 6+6 blades and a 50 mm turbine outlet, retaining the original K16 turbine with blade clipping. These dimensions are supplier data, not complete manufacturing geometry.

TTE advertises 650 PS for its 993 TTE650. The consulted listing contains no complete engine configuration, measured 993 dyno curve, compressor map or turbine map. A linked media archive is named for a 996 product and cannot establish a 993 result.
The TTE750 conversion requires K24 turbochargers and explicitly excludes K16 donors. Its page specifies a 51 mm compressor inlet, a 54 mm turbine outlet and K24/10 hot housings.

The TTE800 uses K24/10 hot housings and a replacement nine-blade turbine/shaft, with a 51 mm compressor inlet and 54 mm turbine outlet. Its more-than-800 PS claim is stated for 102 RON fuel and requires software changes. Maps and a complete operating envelope were not published.

application: TTE general VSR process versus 993 product
text: TTE describes VSR balancing equipment that can reach 250,000 rpm for some applications. This general process statement is not a 250,000 rpm continuous operating limit for the 993 TTE650.

application: BorgWarner 993 stock and upgrade application table
text: BorgWarner lists K16-6735 and K16-6736 for the 993 and prints a stock-turbo limit of 500 hp. The same application table lists upgrade references 5324 988 7003 and 5324 988 7004 with a 555 hp limit. These are catalogue capacity figures, not measured engine curves or compressor/turbine maps.

The BorgWarner 993 upgrade row prints maximum T3 values of 950 degrees C continuously and 980 degrees C temporarily. These values belong to the upgrade table. They do not establish measured stock-K16 exhaust temperature, alloy identity or a safe engine operating target.

Cargraphic lists 475 PS at 6090 rpm and 632 Nm at 4550 rpm for a package containing modified K16/24 turbos and supporting changes to software, exhaust, intake and oil cooling. The consulted page does not publish the plotted test trace, boost trace or turbo maps.
The consulted Turbo Dynamics MD433 page did not establish a 993 donor, wheel geometry, power capacity or compressor/turbine map. A product title alone is insufficient to assert compatibility.
Turbo Technics describes performance and bespoke turbo work. No specific 993 product datasheet or exact 993 map was established from the generic page consulted.

application: Current RUF UK Turbo R rebuild specification
text: The current RUF UK Turbo R page pairs 405 kW with 550 bhp at 5500 rpm and lists 700 Nm at 4800 rpm. The power units disagree: 405 kW is approximately 550.6 PS or 543.1 mechanical hp. Preserve the printed values and flag the inconsistency instead of silently changing the label.

application: Current and historical RUF Turbo R descriptions
text: RUF UK describes a current Turbo R rebuild with its own ignition and engine-management specification. Rstrada lists a historical Turbo R description at 490 hp and 479 lb-ft without the associated rpm on that page. These entries describe different source contexts and should not be merged into one original factory specification.

Rstrada describes 3.6 litre CTR2 and CTR2 Sport engines with different power and torque ratings and charge-air cooling arrangements from a stock 993 Turbo. It does not identify the complete turbo reference or publish compressor/turbine maps.

application: Reported RUF Turbo R chassis-dyno result
text: A Rennlist owner post describes a RUF Turbo R dyno result. An engine or chassis-dyno power curve plots engine output against engine speed. Without turbo inlet/outlet conditions, corrected flow and shaft speed, it cannot uniquely reconstruct a compressor/turbine map.

A forum transcription associates 468 lb-ft with 5500 rpm and separately reports 506 hp near that engine speed. Mechanical horsepower from those torque and rpm values is 468 times 5500 divided by approximately 5252, about 490 hp. The mismatch requires the original test sheet and unit conventions; it must not be silently corrected into a verified dyno curve.

application: SJM KKK 2467 GGA/GGB map, Audi upgrade K16-6717
text: SJM hosts a compressor-map scan for KKK 2467 GGA/GGB associated with turbo 5316 988 6717. The compressor family designation resembles that listed for the 993 K16, but the complete turbo reference and housing equivalence have not been established. It is a comparison lead rather than a validated 993 K16-6735/6736 map.

The inspected SJM scan includes corrected-speed lines reaching 160,000 rpm, efficiency contours and corrected flow. A highest plotted speed line is not automatically a rotor mechanical limit, and the scan does not publish a 993 stock operating envelope.

Turbomap lists numerical compressor and turbine data for a Porsche 996 M96/70 K16-2467G application. The listed data are offered on quotation and were not acquired in this research. Complete turbo identity and correspondence with the 993 M64/60 would need verification.

Garrett lists a 48 mm compressor inducer, 60 mm compressor exducer, 54 mm turbine inducer and 49 mm turbine exducer for G25-550. It also publishes compressor and turbine-flow curves for this turbo family. These data describe Garrett hardware, not a K16 hybrid with a similar wheel diameter.

Garrett explicitly declares a maximum shaft speed of 185,000 rpm for G25-550. This is different evidence from merely reading the largest speed line on an unrelated map. The declaration does not apply to the Porsche K16 rotor.

The G25-550 advertised 300-550 hp range is a single-turbo potential crank-power estimate associated with compressor choke flow. It is not a measured Porsche result or guaranteed output for a particular engine.

Garrett publishes compressor and turbine-flow curves for GT2860RS. Its table gives a rounded 47 mm compressor inducer and a 60 mm compressor exducer. A 60 mm compressor description should not be read as a 60 mm inducer.

BorgWarner publishes an EFR6258 compressor map with a 49 mm inducer and 62 mm outer compressor diameter. The inspected map includes a 168,000 rpm line. The complete EFR uses different hardware from a 993 K16.

BorgWarner publishes an EFR6758 compressor map with a 54 mm inducer and 67 mm outer compressor diameter. The inspected map includes a 154,000 rpm line. This larger compressor comparison does not establish that a K16 housing accepts the wheel or provides the same map.
The SJM Audi K24 map is associated with compressor 2470GGA/6.13 and KKK 53249707000. The family name K24 alone does not establish identity with the Porsche 993 K24 application.
SJM lists the Audi RS2 turbo as KKK 53249707200 with compressor 2672GGC for the ADU five-cylinder engine. Porsche’s historical involvement with RS2 does not make this a 993 Turbo map.

A compressor map relates pressure ratio and corrected mass flow with efficiency contours and corrected shaft-speed lines. Turbine data relate expansion ratio, corrected exhaust flow and, when available, efficiency and speed. A dyno curve relates engine power or torque to engine rpm. ECU maps instead store control targets and calibration values. These are distinct data types.

Compressor pressure ratio uses absolute outlet pressure divided by absolute inlet pressure. For an illustrative manifold pressure of 2.4 bar absolute, 0.1 bar outlet-path loss and 0.95 bar compressor-inlet pressure, the ratio is (2.4+0.1)/0.95, approximately 2.63. These pressures are scenario inputs, not measured Porsche data.

For symmetric parallel twin turbos, each compressor is sized using half the engine’s total air mass flow under the equal-flow assumption. The two compressors each develop the required pressure ratio; their pressure ratios are not added or divided by two.

Corrected-flow and corrected-speed values depend on the map’s pressure and temperature reference convention. In a common convention, m_corrected=m*sqrt(Tin/Tref)/(Pin/Pref), and N_corrected=N/sqrt(Tin/Tref). Use absolute pressure and temperature and the actual map references. A stated corrected speed is not automatically the physical shaft speed.

For an illustrative four-stroke engine, total air flow can be estimated as Vd*n/120*VE*pman/(R*Tman). With Vd=0.0036 m3, n=6000 rpm, VE=0.90, pman=240000 Pa, Tman=323.15 K and R=287.05 J/(kg K), equal sharing gives approximately 0.2096 kg/s per turbo. These are assumed inputs; the result is not a measured M64/60 flow or a predicted horsepower.

Singer’s 2022 Classic Turbo description uses a Type 964-based 3.8 litre engine, electric wastegates and air/water charge cooling. It advertises 450 or 510 HP. The consulted release provides no compressor/turbine map and does not describe a stock 3.6 litre M64/60 K16 configuration.

The 2023 DLS Turbo release describes a Type 964-based 3.8 litre four-valve engine above 700 HP and 9000 rpm. The 2026 Sorcerer description explicitly includes water-cooled heads and variable-geometry turbos, with 710 HP SAE Net. Keep the dated configurations separate; neither consulted release publishes maps for the stock 993 K16.

application: Gunther Werks current 4.0 litre Turbo program
text: The consulted Gunther Werks Turbo page describes a 993-based vehicle with a 4.0 litre twin-turbo engine, horizontal fan, Motec management and an advertised 850 bhp. It does not identify the exact turbo or publish compressor/turbine maps. A 993 body does not establish stock M64/60 internals.

TurboMaster lists the stock 993 pair as K16-2467GGA/8.88 and displays an A/R value of 8.00. The convention behind this number was not established. Size-8 and size-10 KKK housing labels must not be treated automatically as conventional dimensionless Garrett A/R values.

Within each turbo, its compressor and turbine are joined by one shaft and therefore share physical rotational speed. The two turbos are not mechanically synchronized with each other or the crankshaft. Their exact operating speeds were not established by the consulted nomenclature.
